I want to make something clear for everyone asking questions or concerned our SL is always placed in a strategic way. I’m either using the previous hour candles or the main zone. Sometimes a zone is wide, so the SL will be wide. That’s normal

Now remember this very clearly
SL size does NOT matter in risk management.
If you are risking 1%, it’s always 1%.
Whether the stop is 10 pips or 100 pips, you lose the exact same amount.
So don’t over-risk. If you break risk rules, you will never see consistency or real profits

Our wins are always counted by RR, not pips.
If we hit anything above 1:1.5R or TP3, that’s a win.
If you struggle holding runners because of emotions, I recommend closing full at 1:2R. My final TP will always be around 1:3R, sometimes more if I’m planning to scale the position

Keep this in mind.. I only send signals that actually make sense and are worth taking.
We’re not gambling, we’re not revenge trading. My money is on the line too  I will never send trades just to “send something.” I’ll continue sending 3–4 clean setups a day

Your job is to follow proper risk. My own rule is max 2.5% loss per day, meaning if I take two 1% losses, my next setup will be reduced risk. Everyone should follow the same logic. We stay transparent here wins, losses, BE it’s all part of trading no shame at ALL There’s no such thing as a 100% win rate. We show up every day with the same system that’s been working all year. Gold experienced one of the strongest bearish impulses we've seen in weeks. Sellers were in complete control and bearish momentum was aggressive

We didn't.
Why?

Because price was dropping directly into a major Daily/H4 support area around 3970. This wasn't just a random number

It was an area where price had previously reacted multiple times, making it a high-probability demand zone where buyers were likely waiting

Price swept into the zone and sellers continued pushing

But something important happened...
The selling pressure stopped producing new downside

Despite the heavy bearish volume, price couldn't continue lower

That tells us one thing:
The selling was being absorbed by aggressive buyers. Absorption is one of the strongest clues that large players are stepping into the market !!!!!

Once that absorption happened...
Price reclaimed back above the Daily/H4 support

That reclaim completely changed the picture.
Instead of seeing continuation lower...
We now had confirmation that buyers had defended the zone

This is exactly what we wait for.Waiting for price to prove buyers are taking control.

After reclaiming support...
Price began printing highs, broke above stucture 4000 while respecting the new bullish structure

- Momentum shifted.
- Market structure shifted.

Bullish + H4 at that time closing bullish engulfing candle with rejection off lows

Now the 30-minute chart is where execution became easy

Instead of buying after price already exploded...

We waited for price to retrace.
Our Area of Interest wasn't picked randomly.

It was built from confluence:
• Higher-timeframe Daily/H4 support reclaim.
• Fresh bullish order flow.
• Previous resistance becoming support.
• 30min bullish imbalance candle form 
• Fib Placement (golden zone)
• A clean retracement into value after the impulsive move.
• Strong bullish momentum entering NY

That pullback gave us the exact area where institutions were most likely to defend price again. That's where our limit order was sitting.

After tapping our AOI... Buyers immediately stepped back in.
The reaction confirmed exactly what we expected. From there... Gold continued respecting bullish structure and is now running 650+ pips.

The biggest lesson here isn't the 650 pips. It's understanding WHY the trade worked.

Identify where institutions are likely interested
Wait for absorption
Wait for the reclaim
Confirm the shift in structure
Then let the lower timeframes deliver the entry

Guys...

It's a new trading week. But a new week doesn't mean you need to trade harder. It doesn't mean you need to make back what you lost last week.
It doesn't mean you need to prove anything to anyone.

The market doesn't care what happened last week.

It doesn't know you lost.
It doesn't know you won.
It doesn't owe you anything.

Your only job is to show up with the exact same mindset every single day.

Over the years, after repeating this process thousands of times, I've realized something...
Trading is far less about strategy than people think.
It's a mental game.

The charts don't change nearly as much as your emotions do.
When you're winning, you feel unstoppable. You convince yourself that you've figured it all out. Confidence turns into overconfidence, discipline starts slipping, and that's usually where mistakes begin.

Then the opposite happens.

You hit a few losses and suddenly everything changes.

You start doubting your strategy. You hesitate on valid setups. You become fearful, frustrated, confused.

The same system that made you money a few days ago suddenly feels like it doesn't work.

Nothing changed... Only your mindset did.

The traders who last in this business aren't the ones with the best entries.

They're the ones who stay emotionally neutral whether they're up or down.

They stay humble after wins. They stay confident after losses. They don't let one trade define them. They don't let one week define them.

This week, don't chase.
Don't force.
Don't trade with ego.
Trade your plan.
Protect your capital.

Accept that some days you'll win, some days you'll lose, and some days the best trade is no trade at all.

The goal isn't to have the biggest week. The goal is to become the same disciplined trader every single week.

Stay patient.
Stay humble.

Before I enter any position, I need the market to confirm my idea. If that confirmation never comes, then there's no trade. I don't guess, I don't anticipate, and I definitely don't chase

Those candle closes are a big part of my process. They help separate strong setups from weak ones, keep emotions out of the decision, and protect us from taking unnecessary risks

I'd rather watch a move happen without me than force an entry that doesn't meet my plan. There will always be another opportunity. At the end of the day, consistency isn't built by trading more. It's built by trading better

Stay patient, trust the process, and let quality always come before quantity

Let's talk about risk management before our next trade

If you're getting emotional after a loss, it usually means one of two things: you're overrisking more than you should, or you're letting a loss define everything. Both are fixable, and both come down to mindset

Trading with live money is 90% psychology. If your mindset is "I need to make more than my deposit" or "I need to flip this account," that's not a trader's mindset that's a gambler's mindset. And just because you took one loss doesn't mean you double your lot size to "get it back." That's how accounts actually blow up

Keep it simple: 1 trade = 1%, or even 0.5%. If you have $1,000, you're risking $10-$15 not $50, not $100. Same math applies whether you've got $500 or $50,000. The percentage doesn't change just because you're frustrated

Here's something I personally do: I risk an amount I'm genuinely comfortable losing. Say I'm okay losing $100-200 to make $300-400 yes, that's a higher risk trade, but the key word is *comfortable*. If the loss would actually hurt or make you spiral, the size is wrong, full stop

A loss doesn't define anything. It shouldn't make you emotional. Accept it like you'd accept a win, and move on to the next trade with a clear head. That's the difference between someone who lasts in this game and someone who doesn't

We experienced what REAL trading looks like

Some trades didn't go our way
Some limits missed us
NY gave us slower sessions
We made mistakes on a few setups
And we also caught some really solid wins

That's trading

Not every day is going to pay you. Not every week is going to be perfect. And the sooner you accept that, the easier this game becomes mentally. Trust me, I probably feel the urge to take another trade more than anyone here. I want to catch opportunities. I want to give you guys trades. I want us to win

But my job isn't to trade just so VIP stays active. My job is to protect capital first and wait for the same high-probability setups I've trusted for years.

If the setup isn't there, we wait
If price misses our limit, we let it go
If market conditions change, we adapt
If we're wrong, we manage the loss
If we're right, we secure and manage the position

There will ALWAYS be another setup. There will ALWAYS be another session. We don't get paid for being active. We get paid for being disciplined. That's something I really want everyone here to understand

One losing trade shouldn't change your mood
One missed trade shouldn't make you chase
One slow day shouldn't make you increase your risk
And one winning trade shouldn't make you feel invincible

Your job is to execute the same process over and over again

Risk 0.5%-1%. Protect your account. Stop trying to flip accounts overnight. Stop thinking you need to make everything back on the next trade.

If you genuinely want to be in this game for YEARS, you need to think about survival before profit. And that's why throughout every trade I'm constantly updating you guys when I'm entering, when I'm securing, when I'm cutting, when I'm adjusting, when my bias changes and when I'm simply staying OUT

I don't only want you guys to see the winning screenshot. I want you to understand the decisions that happen BEFORE the screenshot. Because that's where the real skill is. We're building traders here, not gamblers.


We take the wins. We learn from the losses. We study the mistakes. Then we come back next session with a CLEAR HEAD. Risk management first. Profits second. Longevity always. 🦾 Enjoy your night, reset, and we'll attack the next session when the market gives us something worth taking 🤝
